chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn ʿUmar, who said:
I asked Abā Al-Ḥasan Al-Riḍā عليه السلام about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
Then We gave the Book as inheritance to those whom We chose from among Our servants.

— the verse. He said: The children of Fāṭimah عليها السلام. And the one foremost in good deeds is the Imam, and the moderate one is the one who recognizes the Imam, and the one who wrongs himself is the one who does not recognize the Imam.

key_terms.أَوْرَثْنَا: We gave as inheritance; indicating the divinely granted inheritance of the Book
key_terms.السَّابِقُ بِالْخَيْرَاتِ: the one foremost in good deeds, interpreted here as the Imam
key_terms.الظَّالِمُ لِنَفْسِهِ: the one who wrongs himself, explained here as one who does not recognize the Imam
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the Imam, the divinely designated guide whose recognition is central in the narration
key_terms.الْكِتَابَ: the Book, referring to divine scripture
key_terms.الْمُقْتَصِدُ: the moderate one, explained here as one who recognizes the Imam
key_terms.وُلْدُ فَاطِمَةَ: the children of Fāṭimah عليها السلام, identified here as the chosen inheritors

ai.seo_question: Who are those chosen to inherit the Book in Qur'an 35:32 according to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse about those who inherit the Book as referring to the descendants of Fāṭimah عليها السلام. It identifies the one foremost in good deeds as the Imam, the moderate one as the one who knows the Imam, and the one who wrongs himself as the one who does not know the Imam. The narration presents recognition of the Imam as central to understanding the ranks mentioned in the verse.
